hero.h1: Trenchless Sewer Repair in Arlington Heights, IL
hero.sub: A failing sewer line doesn't have to mean a trench across your front yard, your driveway and the parkway tree. We line or replace the pipe through small access points, after a camera shows exactly where the damage is. From our office on East Central Road.

img.alt: Two J. Blanton plumbers pouring resin into a sewer liner bag to prepare a trenchless pipe lining

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.body: Trenchless sewer repair, also called no-dig sewer repair, fixes a damaged pipe without digging a trench along its full length. Instead of opening up your yard from the house to the street, we work through one or two access points and repair the pipe from the inside or replace it in place. There are two main methods: cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) lining and pipe bursting. Both fix the line underground, so what's above it stays untouched.

img.alt: Two J. Blanton plumbers setting up sewer camera and cable equipment beside a home's foundation before a trenchless sewer repair

blocks.h2: Why Trenchless Fits Arlington Heights Homes
blocks.intro: Trenchless repair is one of the most searched sewer services in Arlington Heights, and it fits the way homes here are built and landscaped.

items.body: Postwar blocks have trees that are 60 years old or more. Digging a trench next to one can damage the roots and the tree. Lining goes under them.

items.h3: Driveways and Garages in the Path
items.body: Many sewer lines run under a driveway, a walk or a detached garage. Trenchless repair works from both ends and leaves them in place.

items.h3: Clay Joints Failing All at Once
items.body: When roots have opened most of the joints in a clay line, a liner seals every joint in one job instead of fixing them one by one.
Many homes have both. We can often line the outside lateral and deal with the cast iron under the floor separately, so you only fix what's failing.

blocks.h2: Trenchless Sewer Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: Will trenchless repair save my parkway tree?
items.preview: Usually. Lining works inside the old pipe, so the roots stay undisturbed.
items.answer: Usually. A liner goes inside the existing pipe, so nobody digs through the root zone. If roots have crushed the pipe completely, we'll tell you what that changes before any work starts.

items.q: How long does a sewer liner last?
items.preview: Decades. Liners are designed for a long service life.
items.answer: Liners are designed to last for decades. Once cured, the liner is a seamless pipe inside your old one, with no joints for roots to get through.

items.preview: Slightly, but a smooth liner usually flows as well or better.
items.answer: Slightly. A liner adds a thin wall inside the pipe. Because it's smooth and has no joints or scale, it usually carries water as well as the old pipe did when it was new.

items.q: Can you line a sewer that has a sag?
items.preview: A shallow sag, often. A deep one usually needs a spot repair first.
items.answer: A liner follows the shape of the old pipe, so it won't lift a low spot. A shallow sag can often be lined. A deep one is usually fixed with a small dig first, then the rest of the line is lined.

items.q: How much does trenchless sewer repair cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on length, depth and method. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on how much of the line needs work, the depth, the method and access. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
